title: Classify each train with its category field

facts.note: Train definition files authored by the planner.
Fires when a train is added or any part of it (category, identity, steps, acceptance, outcome) is edited.
Planning tasks that author, rename or reclassify trains.

values: train category field set or changed
facts.note: Diff-level observer on train files: detects category edits, identity edits, and semantic edits that may require reclassification.

values: category does not match the scenario's semantics
facts.note: Whether the domain ran / succeeded / refuses deterministically, and whether a name encodes the category, needs semantic judgement.

fires: Planner authors a new train and must set its category.
Planner reclassifies an existing train (e.g. from error to exception).
Planner names or renames a train and might embed its category in the name/id.

Planner edits a train's steps or acceptance so the scenario now ends in a different kind of outcome (e.g. a success path becomes an in-domain refusal or an external fault), which may make the existing category wrong.
doesNotFire: Authoring wagons, WMBTs or docs that do not define trains.
Classifying a train along the separate family axis (governed by planner.train.family).
Purely cosmetic edits to a train (typo, formatting) that change neither its outcome semantics, category nor identity.

given: A planner is authoring or editing a train, including its steps, acceptance or outcome
when: the train is created, named or renamed, or its scenario semantics change in a way that may alter its category
then: Set the train's `category` field to exactly one of nominal, error, alternate or exception, chosen by the category definitions.
prefer: nominal: the intended journey; the domain runs to completion and returns the outcome the job exists to produce.
alternate: another in-domain route to success (input mode, channel, configuration, persona); a success, not a failure.
exception: the domain ran and refused (negative verdict, the business rule working); retry is refused identically (validation, rule violations, policy denials).
error: fault outside the domain; domain never ran, no verdict or postcondition; retry may succeed once the fault clears (crashes, collaborator unavailability, infrastructure).
Reclassify by editing the category field, without a category-driven rename.
avoid: Encoding the category in the train's name or id (category is metadata, not identity).
Labelling a business-rule refusal as error, or an alternate success as a failure.
why: Category is metadata, not identity, so a train is reclassified by changing a field rather than its name; the closed set keeps success, in-domain refusal and out-of-domain fault distinct.
evidence: Each train has a `category` field whose value is one of nominal, error, alternate, exception; no other value is used.
The train's name/id does not encode its category, and a reclassification is expressed as a change of the category field without requiring a rename (other unrelated edits in the same change are fine).

Reviewer checks the chosen value against the definitions: did the domain run, did it succeed, is a refusal deterministic on retry; when steps/acceptance change the outcome, the category is re-checked.
verifier_detail: Term `category` (label 'Test categories'), defined as name -> description: the four values of the train's `category` field. Closed set: nominal, error, alternate, exception; value keys are unchanged from legacy.

Full definitions. nominal: The intended journey - the domain runs to completion and returns the outcome the job exists to produce. error: Failure originating outside the modelled domain - the domain never ran, so no verdict exists and no domain postcondition holds; the identical request may succeed once the fault clears (crashes, collaborator unavailability, infrastructure faults). alternate: A different in-domain route to a successful outcome - another input mode, channel, configuration or persona; still a success, not a failure. exception: An in-domain refusal - the domain ran, evaluated the request and rendered a negative verdict, so the refusal is the business rule working; the identical request is refused identically on retry (validation failures, business rule violations, policy denials).
